matrix_ledger._doc: R4 trace for L-MATRIX-LEDGER (queen order trios#380, P0 cascade-blocker). Every numeric column in assertions/matrix_samples.jsonl traces back to the file in THIS repository that produces it, cited below. Anchor: phi^2 + phi^-2 = 3.
matrix_ledger._witness_status: RETRACTED 2026-08-03. Every row currently in assertions/matrix_samples.jsonl is retracted and none may be cited as a measurement. The 20 rows were produced by GHA run 25539291483 at commit 4e861b3, where cpu_train read the hardcoded path data/tinyshakespeare.txt, the /data/ directory was gitignored, and the format-algo-matrix workflow had no step that fetched or created any corpus. load_data therefore fell through to its 52-byte literal fallback, "Hello world this is a tiny training dataset for IGLA". With --vocab=128 an untrained model scores log2(128) = 7.0 bpb exactly, which is what the rows report: 15 of 20 sit on 7.000391960144043 or 7.000393390655518 with delta_bpb 0.0, and falsifier_2_hit is true on 20 of 20. See the per-row retraction fields in that file.

forbidden_seeds._history: Until 2026-08-03 this key was `forbidden_seeds_painted` and the ledger REWROTE the band (42->47, 43->89, 44->144, 45->123) into a column named `seed_phi`, emitting no seed_raw and no painted flag. Because 47/89/144/123 are themselves legitimate canon seeds, a repainted row was indistinguishable from a genuine run at the target seed; the only trace was an eprintln to a GitHub Actions log that expires. The repaint helper in src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs is deleted, the column is now `seed`, copied verbatim from cell.json, and a seed in the band aborts the collect run with exit code 4.
forbidden_seeds._proof_citation_audit: This block previously carried a "_proof" key naming a Coq theorem (spelled 'forbidden seed repaint') in a file t27/proofs/forbidden-seeds.v, and the loss_final column trace named a second file t27/proofs/bpb-loss-isomorphism.v. Both were searched for on 2026-08-03 in the t27 checkout at /Users/playra/t27. `ls /Users/playra/t27/proofs` lists CoqMakefile, CoqMakefile.conf, README.md, _CoqProject and the subdirectories gravity/, lean4/, sacred/, trinity/ (335 files in total). A recursive grep for both theorem names across the whole checkout returned no match (exit 1), and `find /Users/playra/t27 -iname '*forbidden*'` returned nothing. Neither file exists, so both citations are removed rather than repaired, and their exact identifiers are deliberately not reproduced here so that a grep for the citation finds nothing. The seed policy is a Rust guard with a unit test, not a proven theorem, and must not be presented as one.

matrix_ledger._column_trace_doc: Every entry names the file in THIS repository that produces the column. This is a single-crate repository (package `trios-trainer`) whose sources live directly under src/ and src/bin/. The previous entries pointed at a nested crates/<crate>/src/... workspace layout that does not exist here, so none of those paths resolved.

column_trace.cell_id: derived(format, algo, seed) in src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs::parse_one; a reproducible identifier, not a measurement
column_trace.format: REQUESTED format only. src/bin/matrix_runner.rs::normalize_format canonicalizes the --format string and forwards it as TRIOS_FORMAT_TYPE; this column is that string. It is NOT provenance of the executed kernel -- src/bin/cpu_train.rs resolves FormatKind::from_env(...).unwrap_or(FormatKind::F32), so an unrecognized spelling silently trains in f32. The executed kernel is reported by the separate `format_executed` column; read that one when you need to know what ran. Contract: matrix_runner R5-REJECTs a cell whose cpu_train run reports no `format_executed`, or one that disagrees with the request. The 20 rows in matrix_samples.jsonl predate `format_executed` and therefore state a request with no record of the execution.
column_trace.format_executed: src/bin/cpu_train.rs result JSON key `format_executed` -- the FormatKind the trainer actually ran, carried through src/bin/matrix_runner.rs and src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs::parse_one. An empty string means the artifact predates the field and is reported as such, never guessed.
column_trace.algo: src/bin/cpu_train.rs::AlgoOpt::from_env -- 9 variants (adamw, muon, sgdm, lion, adafactor, lamb, schedulefree, rmsprop, soap). It panics on an unknown name rather than falling back, so unlike `format` this column does reflect the optimizer that ran. Requests are narrowed upstream by src/bin/matrix_runner.rs::ALGO_WHITELIST, currently ["adamw", "muon"]. The earlier citation of src/optimizer.rs::OptimizerKind was wrong: that library type is not used by cpu_train.
column_trace.seed: src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs::parse_one -- copied verbatim from cell.json::seed, which src/bin/matrix_runner.rs took from --seed. No transform is applied. See `forbidden_seeds` above for the deleted repaint and for the removed proof citation.
column_trace.hidden: src/bin/cpu_train.rs --dim argument, forwarded by src/bin/matrix_runner.rs::run_cpu_train from --hidden (lr/h scale invariants)
column_trace.step: src/bin/cpu_train.rs --steps argument, echoed back through the result JSON. This is the REQUESTED step count; it is the step at which `bpb` was measured, and it is NOT the step at which `best_bpb` occurred.
column_trace.bpb: src/bin/cpu_train.rs result key `final_bpb` -- the value measured at step == steps. Correction: before 2026-08-03 cpu_train emitted the running MINIMUM over all evals under the name `final_bpb`, and this entry documented it as "real BPB". Rows written before that date therefore carry a minimum labelled as a final measurement, which overstates any run that diverged after its best step.
column_trace.best_bpb: src/bin/cpu_train.rs result key `best_bpb` -- the minimum over all evaluated steps, at a step that is not recorded. Carried beside `bpb` so the two are visibly distinct numbers. Absent in pre-2026-08-03 artifacts, where it defaults to 0.0.
column_trace.initial_bpb: src/bin/cpu_train.rs::init_bpb -- bpb measured before the first optimizer step (warmup baseline)
column_trace.delta_bpb: derived(initial_bpb - bpb) in src/bin/cpu_train.rs; carries no information beyond its two operands. In pre-2026-08-03 artifacts it was init_bpb - best_bpb, i.e. an upper bound on the improvement actually held at the end of training.
column_trace.loss_final_derived: derived(bpb * ln 2) in src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs::parse_one. Carries NO independent information: it is the `bpb` column restated in nats, and was verified byte-identical to bpb*ln2 on all 20 committed rows. Do not average, plot or cite it alongside `bpb` as if it were a second measurement. The previous entry named this column `loss_final` and cited a Coq file under t27/proofs for the convention; that file does not exist (see forbidden_seeds._proof_citation_audit), and bpb = loss / ln 2 is a unit definition, not a theorem, so the citation is removed.
column_trace.commit_sha: cell.json::sha (git rev-parse --short HEAD in src/bin/matrix_runner.rs), else GITHUB_SHA -- points the cell at a reproducible source state
column_trace.workflow_run_id: cell.json::run_id, else GITHUB_RUN_ID -- joins to GHA logs at /actions/runs/<id>
column_trace.falsifier_2_hit: src/bin/matrix_ledger.rs::falsifier_2_hit. R7 witness for AP.B Falsifier-2 (IGLA-track); flips when bpb > 1.85 OR the derived loss is NaN/Inf/>=1e6. Note the second clause is the first restated in nats, not an independent check, so this boolean is a function of `bpb` alone. A parse_error row sets it true because the cell cannot be shown to have stayed below Gate-2.

falsifier_2.name: AP.B-F2 IGLA-track Gate-2
falsifier_2.clause: Refuted iff some cell has bpb > 1.85 OR loss_final_derived NaN/Inf/>=1e6. The second disjunct is the first restated in nats, so the predicate is a function of bpb alone.
falsifier_2.witness_status: NO VALID WITNESS ON DISK. The 20 rows at witness_path are retracted (see _witness_status above): they were measured on a 52-byte fallback corpus, so their falsifier_2_hit=true means the training data was absent, not that Gate-2 was refuted by a real run. A falsifier that fires on a missing corpus is not evidence about the model. This clause has no witness until the matrix is re-run against a named, hash-pinned corpus.
